title: LP2-15: prime-only totient and Fibonacci-gap proposal
question: Does the reported totient-before-prime-gap sequence reconstruct all sixteen LP2-15 cells and its own Fibonacci-gap array under one stated rule?
summary: The source's totient array matches all sixteen cells after changing only prime 3299 to 3298. Its prime candidates require two addition choices despite a subtraction label; fourteen of fifteen specified predecessor gaps match, while one reports 317 instead of 377.

scope.representation: The printed 4×4 decimal panel and all three 4×4 source arrays preserved in plan.json, including one question mark.
scope.procedure: Apply phi to printed prime cells, enumerate 3301 ± each result, independently compute prime ordinals and compare the posted predecessor-Fibonacci gaps without repairing them.
scope.parameters: All sixteen image-order cells; base 3301; both signs logged; zero-based prime indices; source-stated cells compared individually. No rune operation.
scope.exclusions: No interpretation of the missing screenshot, inferred decryption method, rune shift, selective omission of the duplicate 3 or correction of 317 in the source array.

finding: The first array matches 16/16; the second matches 16/16 with two plus signs. Primality alone leaves two ambiguous sign cells. All selected candidates have Fibonacci-valued prime indices, but index 1 is duplicated and index 0 absent. The final array matches 14/15 specified predecessor gaps, with row 4 column 1 inconsistent and row 2 column 2 uncertain.
limitations: This is a source-bound reconstruction of derived arithmetic, not an independent construction of the printed panel or a cipher test. The source supplies no complete rune transformation, and its sign-selection and repeated-one assignment are not fixed as forward rules.
next_steps: A future decoding proposal must freeze its sign rule, the treatment of duplicate prime 3, the 317/377 disagreement, a panel traversal, rune operation and untouched validation target before inspecting plaintext.
